payload.passage: Greenfield Library will close for three weeks this autumn while workers build a new children's section. The council announced the plan on Monday. The work will cost about 200,000 pounds, and most of the money comes from a local business, Hartley Foods. During the closure, readers can borrow books from a mobile library, a van that will park outside the town hall every weekday morning. payload.passage: Three months ago I could only make toast and boiled eggs. My friends laughed at me, so I decided to learn to cook properly. At first I followed videos online, but they went too fast and I burned a lot of food. Then I joined a Tuesday evening class at the community centre. Our teacher, Marco, shows us each step slowly and lets us taste everything. Last week I made a vegetable soup for my parents, and my dad asked for a second bowl! I still can't make good bread, which is my next goal. If you're thinking about learning something new, my advice is simple: find a real person to learn from. It's much easier than watching a screen.

payload.passage: Several companies in Britain have recently been testing a four-day working week, and the early results are surprising. In one trial involving more than sixty firms, employees kept their full salaries but worked only thirty-two hours instead of forty. Many managers had expected productivity to fall. In fact, most companies reported that output stayed the same, and a few even saw it rise. Workers said they felt less stressed and slept better, and the number of people calling in sick dropped noticeably. However, the scheme did not suit everyone. Some employers in customer service found it hard to keep their offices staffed on the days when customers needed help, and a handful of employees admitted that the compressed schedule left them exhausted by the end of the week. Researchers stress that the results come from voluntary participants, who were probably already positive about the idea. They therefore advise caution before drawing wider conclusions, although most of the firms involved have decided to continue with the new schedule.
payload.question: What did many managers anticipate before the trial began?
options: Salaries would have to be raised
Their companies would produce less work
Workers would ask for longer holidays
payload.explanation_uz: Matnda: "Many managers had expected productivity to fall" - ish unumdorligi tushadi deb kutishgan.

payload.passage: When I moved to Canada for my master's degree, I assumed my English was good enough. I had passed my exams with high marks, after all. Within a week, I realised how wrong I was. People spoke quickly, used slang I had never met, and seemed to leave half of every sentence unfinished. In seminars I understood the words but missed the jokes, which made me feel strangely invisible. What changed things was not a course or an app, but a part-time job in a bookshop. Customers asked me for recommendations, and I was forced to improvise, explain and sometimes admit I hadn't understood. My colleagues corrected me gently, and within three months I stopped translating in my head. I still make mistakes, and I still get nervous on the phone, but I no longer think of fluency as a finish line. It is more like a path that keeps stretching ahead, and the best way to walk it is among people who are happy to talk.

payload.passage: In recent years, a growing number of cities have encouraged residents to keep bees on rooftops and balconies. At first glance this may seem risky, but experts say that urban hives often produce more honey than those in the countryside. The reason is variety: gardens, parks and even window boxes provide flowers throughout the year, whereas farmland dominated by a single crop offers food for only a few weeks. Pesticides are also used less intensively in town. Nevertheless, some biologists warn that the trend has a downside. Honeybees compete for nectar with wild species such as bumblebees, which are already in decline and cannot be managed by humans. Dr Karen Holt, who studies pollinators, argues that planting more flowers matters more than adding more hives. "If we simply increase the number of honeybees without increasing food, we help the species that needs help least," she says. Several councils are now rethinking their schemes, offering free seeds instead of subsidised hives.
payload.question: Why do city hives often produce more honey than rural ones?
options: City bees are a stronger species
Beekeepers in towns are better trained
The weather in cities is warmer
Flowers are available over a much longer period

payload.transcript: Welcome back to Healthy Habits. Today I want to challenge a popular myth: that we can catch up on lost sleep at weekends. Many of us sleep five or six hours on weekdays, then stay in bed until noon on Saturday, believing the debt is paid. Research from a Colorado university suggests otherwise. People who slept late at weekends still showed poorer concentration on Monday. The better strategy, the scientists say, is consistency: going to bed and getting up at roughly the same time every day. If that's impossible, a nap in the early afternoon can help, but keep it to twenty minutes, or you may wake up groggy.
